-    return [list(graph)]
+    """Return deterministic parallel execution waves for *graph*.
+
+    The graph is validated in its entirety before selecting the requested
+    target closure.  All bookkeeping uses new sets/dicts so neither argument
+    is modified.
+    """
+    # Copy dependencies while validating references.  Using sets also makes
+    # duplicate dependency names harmless.
+    names = set(graph)
+    dependencies = {}
+    for name, prerequisites in graph.items():
+        deps = set(prerequisites)
+        if not deps <= names:
+            raise ValueError("unknown dependency")
+        dependencies[name] = deps
+
+    # Kahn's algorithm validates cycles across the whole graph, not merely
+    # the part needed by the requested targets.
+    remaining = {name: set(deps) for name, deps in dependencies.items()}
+    while remaining:
+        ready = {name for name, deps in remaining.items() if not deps}
+        if not ready:
+            raise ValueError("dependency cycle")
+        for name in ready:
+            del remaining[name]
+        for deps in remaining.values():
+            deps.difference_update(ready)
+
+    if targets is None:
+        selected = set(names)
+    else:
+        requested = set(targets)
+        if not requested <= names:
+            raise ValueError("unknown target")
+        selected = set()
+        pending = list(requested)
+        while pending:
+            name = pending.pop()
+            if name in selected:
+                continue
+            selected.add(name)
+            pending.extend(dependencies[name] - selected)
+
+    waves = []
+    completed = set()
+    while selected - completed:
+        wave = sorted(
+            name for name in selected - completed
+            if dependencies[name] <= completed
+        )
+        # The full graph was already checked, so this is only a defensive
+        # guard against an inconsistent input object changing mid-call.
+        if not wave:
+            raise ValueError("dependency cycle")
+        waves.append(wave)
+        completed.update(wave)
+    return waves
